build.#files: Deliberately absent, so wireit runs cargo every time. The binary lands in the workspace target dir (../../target/release/zena-run), which wireit does not track, so a script with inputs and no outputs can be restored from the GitHub Actions cache as fresh on a machine whose target dir is empty. The four scripts that run ../../target/release/zena-run then fail with exit 127. cargo is a fast no-op when its own fingerprints are current.

test.#command: --release reuses the dependency artifacts the build step produced instead of compiling wasmtime a second time in the dev profile.
